To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the failure rates of MODIS MLP cloud property retrievals are higher over the broken cloud regimes than over the stratocumulus regions, and the leading causes of the failed retrievals are due to the large r e and/or small τ values that are outside the LUT, followed by the partial cloudiness and subpixel inhomogeneities of the cloud field, the special Sun‐satellites viewing geometries such cloudbow, and the cloud phase retrieval errors.

the MODIS MLP cloud retrievals are most likely to fail in the broken trade cumulus regime, in partially cloudy pixels, in pixels with large viewing or solar angles, in pixels with high subpixel inclusions, and in pixels that are precipitating.
MODIS retrieval failure rate is about 16% over global oceans, with higher rates over the broken trade cumulus regimes.

the frequency and potential reasons of failed MODIS MLP cloud retrievals and provides useful insights into improving future MODIS retrievals.
the frequency and causes of failed cloud microphysical retrievals over global oceans, which is an important issue for the quality assessment and application of MODIS cloud property products.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the majority of failed MODIS MLP retrievals are due to cloud inhomogeneity and/or cloud overlapping, and the rest is due to the presence of precipitation or the extreme r e values.
the majority of MODIS MLP retrieval failures can be attributed to the limitations of current MODIS cloud products.

the majority of failed MODIS r e and τ retrievals for MLP clouds over the oceans are likely due to the cloud inhomogeneity and/or partial cloudiness, cloud phase retrieval, or precipitation, and that a significant fraction is still due to the MODIS retrieval algorithm limitations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

MODIS retrieval failure rates for MLP clouds are generally low, but they are enhanced in the presence of cloud heterogeneity and at special Sun‐cloud geometries, and they are also associated with precipitation.

the MODIS cloud property retrieval failures over global oceans are mostly due to the partial cloudiness, inhomogeneity, and/or cloud overlapping of MLP clouds and the special Sun‐satellites viewing geometry.
most failed retrievals can be attributed to either cloud inhomogeneity or cloud phase issues, which can be mitigated by using more advanced cloud property retrieval algorithms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the failure rate of MODIS MLP cloud retrievals is not as high as previously reported, especially when the MODIS 2.1/3.7 μm combination is used.
the MODIS retrieval failure rates are not random but rather are related to specific physical conditions.
the MODIS cloud property retrieval failure rate is not negligible.
